terms.gloss: because of, due to, on account of
evidence: Caes. BG 1.16.2: nam propter frīgora … nōn modo frūmenta in agrīs mātūra nōn erant
Cic. Att. 7.5.2: propter hūmānitātem et modestiam mālō salvum quam propter ūsum meum
terms.comment: The plain word for a cause, and the chief sense of propter (Lewis & Short). With persons, “because of me, thanks to you”: propter mē, propter tē.

terms.gloss: because of, for (a reason, a deed)
evidence: Ter. Ad. 978–978b: Ob eam rem? — Ob eam.
Cic. Rep. 1.12: ob eam causam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Mostly in set phrases: ob eam rem, for that reason; quam ob rem, which is why.

terms.grammar: preposition with the ablative, with a negative
evidence: Cic. Att. 9.12.1: prae lacrimīs possum reliqua nec cōgitāre nec scrībere
terms.comment: Classically only of a hindrance, with a negative or vix (Lewis & Short): one cannot speak for tears, see for the crowd.

phrases.latin: nam propter frīgora … nōn modo frūmenta in agrīs mātūra nōn erant
phrases.english: for due to the cold … the corn in the fields was not even ripe

phrases.latin: Ut propter mē tibi sit melius mihique propter tē et tuōs.
phrases.english: So that you may be better off thanks to me, and I thanks to you and yours.

phrases.latin: prae lacrimīs possum reliqua nec cōgitāre nec scrībere
phrases.english: for tears I can neither think nor write the rest
